brief.subject: IRS fixes opportunity zone reporting rule; credit hearing goes phone-only
brief.headline: IRS Corrects Opportunity Zone Reporting Proposal, Moves Scholarship Credit Hearing to Phone
brief.dek: Corrections land on new opportunity fund reporting rules, a December 15 hearing goes telephonic, and the IRS asks for burden comments.
brief.lede: The IRS issued corrections to its proposed opportunity zone information-reporting rules. Funds, zone businesses and their investors face new statement and filing duties.

sections.heading: Opportunity Zone Reporting Rules Corrected
bullets: The IRS published corrections to proposed regulations REG-116506-25, first released September 11, 2026.
Qualified opportunity funds would file information returns and send statements to investors who dispose of their stakes.
Zone businesses would also owe statements to funds holding interests in them, adding a new reporting layer for small operators.
The proposal also updates how funds get certified and decertified, which matters for anyone raising or holding fund capital.

sections.heading: Scholarship Credit Hearing Goes Phone-Only
bullets: The December 15, 2026 hearing at 10 a.m. ET on REG-117199-25 is now telephonic only.
The rules cover a non-refundable federal credit for donations to scholarship granting organizations.
Business owners weighing year-end giving should track this guidance as it takes shape.

sections.heading: IRS Wants Input on Withholding Systems
bullets: The IRS is seeking public comment on paperwork burden for its QI, WP and WT application and account system.
The request falls under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 and affects intermediaries handling foreign withholding.

sections.heading: Texas Climbs Tax Competitiveness Ranking
bullets: Texas rose two spots in the Tax Foundation's latest Tax Competitiveness rankings.
Its lack of a state income tax earned high marks, a factor for owners comparing where to base a business.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures; Correction
items.snippet: This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.
